correctness.rationale: The standard one-third truncation reconstructs 60 vertices, 90 edges, and 30 antipodal vertex pairs. The supplied exact checker uses integer pairs in Q(phi) with phi^2=phi+1 to establish 435 distinct projective pair intersections of 30 great circles (all exactly double), hence 872 chambers. At each intersection it enumerates all four infinitesimal sectors, records 872 distinct sign vectors, and exhaustively counts sign-changing edges in every chamber: multiplicities 132,420,180,120,20 for 10,12,14,16,18 polygon sides. It also certifies one open-cell integer normal per count. The proof explains why edge crossings correspond bijectively to section vertices and why no chamber is missed. Mean N follows from 90 edges subtending one common central angle alpha and P(crossing)=alpha/pi. The full decoded verify.py executes successfully from its package path, printing ALL_CHECKS_PASSED; the finite classification uses exact arithmetic, not simulation.
